questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stop insect bites from becoming painful
Why we feel itchy and whether itching can spread between people
Which clothes are best for people with sensitive skin
How doctors treat serious skin diseases
questions.why: They hear from experts about why we itch and whether you can 'catch' an itch from others.

questions.q: Why is Georgie feeling itchy at the start of the programme?
options: She was bitten by a mosquito on the way to work
She has a skin allergy to a new soap she used
She has just been sitting out in the hot sun
She is wearing a jumper that makes her itch
questions.why: Georgie says she's wearing quite an itchy jumper that makes her want to scratch.

options: An insect bit him and he scratched a lot
He got a rash from a new jumper
He caught a cold from a colleague
He hurt his skin by scratching too hard
questions.why: Neil says he was bitten by a mosquito and had to scratch 'loads and loads'.

questions.q: According to Sonja Ständer, what is the purpose of scratching?
options: To make the skin warmer
To help the skin grow faster
To remove things from the skin that could harm it
To show other people that we feel uncomfortable
questions.why: She says scratching removes parasites, plants or anything that doesn't belong on the skin.

questions.q: Why does Neil find it interesting that talking about itching makes Georgie feel itchy?
options: Because it is exactly what one researcher wanted to study
Because he feels the opposite way
Because it proves she is allergic to her jumper
Because Sonja Ständer said it never happens
questions.why: Neil says Henning Holle wanted to study whether just thinking about itching makes us itchier.

questions.q: What did Henning Holle's team ask people to do in their study?
options: Wear itchy clothes for a whole day
Stop scratching for as long as possible
Listen to experts talking about skin
Watch videos of people itching and scratching
questions.why: Henning and his team studied what happened when people watched videos of itching and scratching.

questions.q: What did the study find about the people who watched the videos?
options: They felt much less itchy than they did before
They felt itchier and scratched without thinking
They only scratched when someone asked them to
They could not tell which body part was scratched
questions.why: Henning says the videos made people feel itchier and they scratched themselves 'more spontaneously'.

questions.q: What does Henning conclude from his research?
options: Scratching is always bad for the skin, so stop
Only people with very hairy skin feel itchy
An itch can pass between people, like an illness
Itching is caused mainly by tiny skin parasites
questions.why: He says 'you can catch a scratch', and Georgie compares it to catching an illness.
